title: Position: Agentic AI Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI
claim: A single monolithic learner peaks narrowly on trained tasks, while a composed multi-component system covers more tasks above the usability threshold, approaching human-level breadth.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right task axis, dashed threshold line with bracketed ranges below
description: A single schematic plot with task spectrum on the x-axis and intelligence level on the y-axis. A thick purple arch represents human intelligence. A red multi-peaked curve labeled Agentic AI rises and falls across the spectrum. Two narrow blue dashed bell curves labeled Monolithics peak only in the middle. A horizontal dashed black line marks the Usability Threshold, and a black line at the top marks Universally Perfect Intelligence. Vertical dotted lines drop from the threshold crossings to the x-axis. Below the axis, colored double-headed arrows mark the ranges: red Expanded on both sides, blue Specific Tasks in the middle, and purple Real-world Tasks spanning the full width. The eye goes first to the tall red and purple curves, then to the narrow blue peaks.
caption: Agentic AI expands the range of usable tasks and improves performance compared to monolithic models. While monolithic models exhibit narrow performance peaks only on specific tasks they are trained for, Agentic AI demonstrates multi-peak performance across a broader spectrum. This expands usable capabilities, approaching and even surpassing the altitude and breadth of human intelligence.
abstract: Is monolithic scaling the only path to AGI? This paper challenges the dogma that purely scaling a single model is sufficient to achieve Artificial General Intelligence. Instead, we identify Agentic AI as a necessary paradigm for mastering the complex, heterogeneous distribution of real-world tasks. Through rigorous theoretical derivations, we contrast the optimization constraints of monolithic learners against the efficiency of Agentic systems, progressing from simple routing mechanisms to general Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topologies. We demonstrate that Agentic AI achieves exponentially superior generalization and sample efficiency. Finally, we discuss the connection to Mixture-of-Experts, reinterpret the instability of current multi-agent frameworks, and call for greater research focus on Agentic AI.
